user.title: SolarSplit
user.description: Choose the grid sensors and the global settings of the surplus control loop.

data_description.export_sensor: Power exported to the grid, in W. With the import sensor, instead of a signed grid sensor.
data_description.import_sensor: Power imported from the grid, in W. With the export sensor, instead of a signed grid sensor.
data_description.pv_sensor: PV production, in W. Needed for zero-injection mode.
data_description.zero_injection_entity: When this entity is on, the inverter limits export and the loop probes loads instead.
data_description.global_condition: When this entity is off, the loop switches off the loads it switched on that respect it, and leaves the rest as they are.
data_description.cycle_interval: How often the control loop runs.
data_description.safety_margin: Power never handed out to loads.
data_description.smoothing_window: Moving average applied to the readings to filter clouds and spikes.
data_description.settle_time: Wait after a change before the next one.
data_description.on_margin: Extra power a load needs, above its own, to be switched on.
data_description.import_tolerance: Grid import tolerated before a load is switched off.
data_description.shadow_mode: Decide and publish decisions without switching any load. Turn off only when the decisions look right.
data_description.stale_timeout: A non-zero grid reading not reported for longer than this, or both grid sensors quiet, counts as unknown and the loop decides nothing. 0 disables the check.
data_description.grid_sensor: One sensor with the grid power, export and import with opposite signs. Use either this one or both the export and import sensors. With one sensor, a reading not reported within the stale data timeout is unknown.
data_description.grid_sign: Only for the signed grid sensor: whether export is negative or positive.
data_description.season_entity: Optional input select or select with the current season. Loads can be limited to some of its options.
data_description.buy_price_sensor: Price of the energy bought, in €/kWh, with the attributes price_00h…price_23h (for example the PVPC sensor of the ESIOS integration). Tomorrow's prices are read from price_next_day_00h… when published; until then the same hour of today is the estimate. Empty: no prices, and grid fill uses the last hours before each deadline.
data_description.sell_price_sensor: Price of the energy exported, in €/kWh, with the same attributes. An hour with expected surplus costs this price; empty: it costs nothing.
data_description.contracted_power: Grid power you may draw. Loads filling their minimum from the grid never take the import over this power less the margin, in the plan and live. 0: unknown, only one load fills from the grid at a time.
data_description.grid_margin: Power kept below the contracted power for the rest of the house while loads fill from the grid.
data_description.solar_forecast_entries: Forecast.Solar entries (or other integrations with a solar forecast for the Energy dashboard), summed: for example one per string. The expected surplus of an hour is the forecast less the house's base load at that hour. Empty, or without data for an hour: the surplus seen at that hour on the last days.
data_description.base_load: House consumption without SolarSplit's loads used at an hour with a forecast before that hour has been learned. It is learned per hour (median of the last 7 days) from the PV power sensor and the grid readings, less the power of every load.
data_description.solar_entity: Binary sensor that is on while there is solar production, for example a threshold helper on the PV power. Without production surplus management does not apply: SolarSplit switches nothing on by surplus, leaves loads it did not switch on alone (on-demand requests, loads switched on by hand or by automations) and gives regulable loads their maximum back; it only switches off the loads it switched on by surplus when the surplus is gone, and grid fill follows its plan. Unknown or unavailable: no production.
data_description.solar_threshold: Without a solar production entity, the PV power sensor decides: production above this power, and none below it less 50 W. Without either, the rule does not apply.
data_description.maintenance_entity: Script, input boolean, binary sensor or switch that is on while devices are being updated (for example the script that updates every ESPHome device). While it is on, and for the margin after, SolarSplit does not learn from the readings (base load and surplus per hour, power from the circuit, saturation of regulable loads). Without it, a device of a load that goes unavailable and comes back within 15 minutes, or restarts, opens the same window. Safety decisions do not change.
data_description.maintenance_margin: Minutes the maintenance window lasts after the entity goes off, a device comes back or restarts: devices restart after their update.

data_description.name: Shown on the load's device.
data_description.entity_id: Switch, input boolean or climate entity that turns the load on and off. For a regulable load, the switch in front of it: SolarSplit never switches it, and while it is off the load is blocked.
data_description.nominal_power: Power the load draws when on.
data_description.power_sensor: Measured power of the load. When set, it is used instead of the nominal power. Required for a regulable load.
data_description.circuit_sensor: Power of the circuit the load is on, shared with other loads (for example an IoTaWatt channel). Without its own power sensor, the load's power is learned from the jumps of the circuit when it switches and, after 3 measurements, used instead of the nominal power.
data_description.no_skip: Only switch on when every eligible load before it is on.
data_description.on_delay: The surplus must cover the load for this long before it is switched on.
data_description.off_delay: The deficit must last this long before the load is switched off.
data_description.min_on: Never switch off sooner after switching on. Protects compressors and pumps.
data_description.min_off: Never switch on sooner after switching off.
data_description.respect_global_condition: When the global condition is off, switch this load off if SolarSplit switched it on; otherwise leave it as it is. Untick for loads that must keep running, such as a pool pump.
data_description.condition_entity: The load is only used while this entity has the state below.
data_description.condition_state: State the usage condition entity must have, for example on.
data_description.respect_manual: If someone else switches the load, stop controlling it until it returns to the state SolarSplit set. Ignored for on-demand loads.
data_description.variable_entity: Relay loads only. While this entity is on, the load is regulated elsewhere: SolarSplit never switches it, but its power counts. For a diverter, use the Regulable type instead.
data_description.load_type: Relay: SolarSplit switches it on and off. Regulable: the device regulates itself (a diverter) and SolarSplit only writes its power limit; fill in the Regulable load section.

control.name: Manual control, season and urgency
control.description: On demand, automatic return to management, seasons in which the load is used, and urgency.

data_description.on_demand: The load is only used while someone asks for it: switching it on from anywhere else (a person, an automation, a remote) starts a request, and switching it off from anywhere else ends it. While the request lasts SolarSplit switches it off when the surplus runs out and back on when it returns; a climate gets back the mode, temperature and fan mode that were set. SolarSplit never switches it on without a request. Replaces Respect manual changes.
data_description.auto_manage: When Manage is switched off, it switches back on by itself when the load goes off, or at the time below.
data_description.manage_at: Local time at which Manage switches back on.
data_description.seasons: The load is only used in these seasons of the season entity (global settings). Empty: all year. Out of season it is not used, and SolarSplit switches it off if it switched it on.
data_description.urgency_entity: Binary sensor, input boolean or switch. While it is on, the load uses the urgency priority instead of its normal one or the one until the minimum: for example a water heater that goes first when its plan is at risk. Unknown: not urgent.
data_description.urgency_priority: Priority while the urgency entity is on (1 = first). On a tie, the urgent load goes first.

regulable.name: Regulable load
regulable.description: Only for the Regulable type. While the mode entity has the automatic value, the load's power is surplus: SolarSplit counts it and writes in the limit entity what the loads ahead of it leave (its maximum if there are none). Until it is saturated it keeps what it could take up to its limit, so a load behind it does not start with that. In any other mode its power is grid power and the load is shown as external.

data_description.limit_entity: Number entity with the device's maximum power, for example the diverter's maximum power.
data_description.auto_state: State of the mode entity that means automatic, for example Auto.
data_description.limit_max: SolarSplit never writes more, and writes it back when it stops limiting the load.
data_description.limit_threshold: A new limit is only written when it moves by at least this much, or reaches the minimum or maximum.
data_description.limit_interval: So the device is not flooded with writes.
data_description.output_entity: Optional sensor or number with the device's output in % (for example the diverter's duty). At 99 % or more for a minute the load is saturated: it cannot take more, and the surplus it leaves goes to the loads behind it. Without it, a load that draws well below its limit while surplus is still exported for a minute is saturated (a thermostat cut).

daily_target.name: Daily objective
daily_target.description: Hours the load must run each day: a minimum guaranteed before a deadline (relay loads only) and an optional maximum used only with surplus. The day starts at the day start time. SolarSplit plans the cheapest hours before the deadline for the minimum, sunny or not: a sunny hour costs what its sun would earn exported, the others the buy price. In a planned hour without enough sun it switches the load on from the grid (grid fill). Once the maximum is reached the load is not used until the next day.

data_description.min_hours: Hours guaranteed before the deadline, with the grid if the surplus is not enough. 0: no minimum. Only relay loads.
data_description.min_entity: Input number, number or sensor with the minimum hours. It takes precedence over the fixed value.
data_description.target_hours: Hours per day, only with surplus, if there is no maximum entity. Once reached the load is not used until the next day. 0: no maximum.
data_description.target_entity: Input number, number or sensor with the maximum hours. It takes precedence over the fixed value.
data_description.day_start: Local time at which the objective's day starts and its hours count from zero. For example 17:00 with a deadline of 09:00 uses the night.
data_description.deadline: Local time by which the minimum must be met. Empty: the end of the objective's day.
data_description.deadline_entity: Input datetime, time or timestamp sensor with the deadline, for another integration to publish it. It takes precedence over the fixed value.
data_description.min_priority: Priority while the minimum is not met before the deadline, only in the hours the plan chose; in other hours and afterwards, the normal one. 0: always the normal one.
data_description.window_start: Grid fill uses the hours of this window first (for example 10:00 to make use of partial sun and the low prices at midday), and others only if they are not enough.
data_description.window_end: End of the preferred window. Both or neither.
data_description.hours_sensor: Sensor with the hours on in the objective's day, for example one of history statistics. Empty: SolarSplit's own count since the day start.

error.entity_in_use: This entity already belongs to another load.
error.regulable_incomplete: A regulable load needs a power sensor, a limit entity and a mode entity.
error.limit_range: The minimum limit must be lower than the maximum.
error.minimum_relay_only: A minimum with a deadline is only for relay loads: a regulable load is never switched.
error.window_incomplete: The preferred window needs both a start and an end.

state.settling: Waiting for the last change to settle
state.external: Regulated by the device outside its automatic mode
state.full_power: Full power: nothing ahead of it
state.limited: Limited to what the loads ahead leave
state.grid_fill: Filling the minimum from the grid (cheapest hours)
state.grid_fill_no_price: Filling the minimum from the grid (no prices: last hours)
state.grid_limit: Grid fill would exceed the contracted power
state.no_solar: No solar production: left as it is
